rule: Wraiths drain mire-essence from lit lanterns
texts: When a wraith approaches a lit lantern, the wraith drains mire-essence from the lantern.
Whenever a wraith nears a lit lantern, the wraith pulls mire-essence from the lantern.

fields.sentence: When a wraith approaches a lit lantern, the wraith drains mire-essence from the lantern.
parse: (: approach_drain_rule (Implication (And (Member $x approach) (Agent $x $w) (Member $w wraith) (Theme $x $l) (Member $l lantern) (Member $l lit)) (And (Member (sk_drain $x) drain) (Agent (sk_drain $x) $w) (Theme (sk_drain $x) mire_essence) (Source (sk_drain $x) $l) (During (sk_drain $x) $x))) (STV 1.0 0.9))

review.notes: The one arguable call is `Theme` rather than `Patient` for the drained mire-essence; the instruction set's "when the test is unclear, default to Theme" covers it. "lit" is correctly an adjective (modifier participle) and not the verb `light`, and the whenever routing, Skolem-function consequent, `Source` oblique and anaphoric reuse of the wraith and lantern variables all follow the instruction set.

fields.sentence: Whenever a wraith nears a lit lantern, the wraith pulls mire-essence from the lantern.
parse: (: wraith_near_pull (Implication (And (Member $x wraith) (Member $y lantern) (Member $y lit) (Member $e1 near) (Agent $e1 $x) (Theme $e1 $y)) (And (Member (sk_pull $e1) pull) (Agent (sk_pull $e1) $x) (Theme (sk_pull $e1) mire_essence) (Source (sk_pull $e1) $y) (During (sk_pull $e1) $e1))) (STV 1.0 0.9))

review.notes: The "lit" restriction is carried as a separate descriptive Member atom rather than fused, per the incidental-description rule for participial modifiers, and both definites resolve to their premise variables. Source for "from the lantern" and Theme for the unchanged pulled/neared objects follow the stated tests.

Adjectivally-restricted bare-plural generic correctly routed to a distributing rule with the restriction as a premise conjunct, not fused into a compound (incidental description). The participial modifier stays drained rather than drain, the -ly adverb stays dimly rather than dim, and the bare-generic 0.9/0.9 is right.
